intro: You are standing at the Basilica of St John, a monastery and church in İzmir province from the 6th century AD. Justinian raised this six-domed basilica over the tomb of John, and when it was finished it was the largest church after Hagia Sophia.
history: In the sixth century Justinian raised a cross-plan basilica under six domes over the hill held to hold the tomb of John. When it was finished, only Hagia Sophia was a larger church. Earthquakes and abandonment brought it down in the Seljuk period, and in the twentieth century some of its columns were re-erected.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the tomb chamber and the baptistery, then the narthex and the Gate of Persecution.
facts: Did you know? The plan was laid out so that the tomb of John would fall exactly beneath the crossing of the domes. And when Justinian's basilica was finished, it was the largest church after Hagia Sophia.
outro: This brings our visit to the Basilica of St John to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Pause once more among the columns before you leave. Enjoy your visit.
